# 3×3 Matrix Analysis: Recursive Generation Depth Estimation

**Generated**: 2026-05-15
**Grid**: 3 models × 3 decoding strategies = 9 cells (8 completed, 1 pending)
**Missing**: GPT-2 XL × top-k k=50

## 1. Matrix Coverage

| Model | Nucleus p=0.95 | Temp τ=0.9 | Top-k k=50 |
|-------|---------------|------------|------------|
| Pythia-1.4B | 78.2% (RF) | 76.3% (RF) | 69.6% (RF) |
| OLMo-1B | 78.8% (RF) | 82.0% (RF) | 74.2% (RF) |
| GPT-2 XL | 83.3% (RF) | 85.4% (RF) | — (pending) |

All values are 4-class Random Forest accuracy on held-out test set (1000 samples/depth × 4 depths).

## 2. Signal Strength Summary

- **Mean 4-class RF accuracy**: 78.5% (σ=4.8%, range: 69.6%–85.4%)
- **Best cell**: GPT-2 XL × temp τ=0.9 (85.4%)
- **Worst cell**: Pythia-1.4B × top-k k=50 (69.6%)
- GPT-2 XL consistently strongest across strategies
- Top-k decoding consistently weakest across models

### Cross-Model Ranking

| Strategy | Mean Spearman ρ | Models |
|----------|----------------|--------|
| Nucleus p=0.95 | 0.80 | 3 |
| Temperature τ=0.9 | 0.75 | 3 |
| Top-k k=50 | 0.74 | 2 |

Nucleus sampling yields the most consistent feature rankings across models.

## 3. Pairwise AUC — Depth Discrimination

Adjacent-depth AUC (RF) at threshold=0.80:

| Cell | d0→d1 | d1→d2 | d2→d3 |
|------|-------|-------|-------|
| pythia_nucleus | 0.998 | 0.861 | 0.801 |
| pythia_temp09 | 0.997 | 0.833 | 0.793 |
| pythia_topk50 | 0.993 | 0.752 | 0.692 |
| olmo_nucleus | 0.983 | 0.867 | 0.812 |
| olmo_temp09 | 0.996 | 0.901 | 0.821 |
| olmo_topk50 | 0.993 | 0.831 | 0.736 |
| gpt2xl_nucleus | 0.994 | 0.913 | 0.883 |
| gpt2xl_temp09 | 0.996 | 0.937 | 0.882 |

All cells show d0→d1 AUC > 0.98 (trivially separable). The discriminability bottleneck is always d2→d3.

## 4. Effective Degradation Depth (EDD) Analysis

EDD is the maximum recursion depth at which consecutive-depth AUC remains above a given threshold. This is the primary contribution metric — it quantifies how deep the recursive generation signal persists.

### 4.1 EDD Matrix (threshold=0.80)

| | Nucleus p=0.95 | Temp τ=0.9 | Top-k k=50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pythia-1.4B | 3 | 2 | 1 |
| OLMo-1B | 3 | 3 | 2 |
| GPT-2 XL | 3 | 3 | — (pending) |

### 4.2 Top-k Systematically Reduces EDD

Top-k decoding produces the lowest EDD across all models:
- **Pythia topk50 is the only EDD=1 cell** (d1→d2 AUC=0.752, below threshold). The degradation signal saturates by depth 2.
- OLMo topk50 achieves EDD=2 but not 3 (d2→d3 AUC=0.736).
- **Interpretation**: top-k's hard vocabulary truncation limits lexical diversity in generated text. With fewer token choices at each step, the statistical features that distinguish recursion depths converge more quickly, causing the discriminative signal to decay faster than under nucleus or temperature sampling.

### 4.3 EDD Threshold Sensitivity

| Threshold | Mean EDD | Cells at EDD=3 | Cells at EDD≤1 |
|-----------|----------|----------------|----------------|
| 0.65 | 3.00 | 8/8 | 0/8 |
| 0.70 | 2.88 | 7/8 | 0/8 |
| 0.75 | 2.75 | 6/8 | 0/8 |
| 0.80 | 2.50 | 5/8 | 1/8 |

Full threshold × cell matrix:

| Cell | τ=0.65 | τ=0.70 | τ=0.75 | τ=0.80 |
|------|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| pythia_nucleus | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| pythia_temp09 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 2 |
| pythia_topk50 | 3 | 2 | 2 | 1 |
| olmo_nucleus | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| olmo_temp09 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| olmo_topk50 | 3 | 3 | 2 | 2 |
| gpt2xl_nucleus | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| gpt2xl_temp09 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 |

- **Most sensitive**: pythia_topk50 (EDD range=2 across thresholds, drops from 3→1)
- **Least sensitive**: 5 cells maintain EDD=3 at all thresholds (pythia_nucleus, olmo_nucleus, olmo_temp09, gpt2xl_nucleus, gpt2xl_temp09)
- At τ=0.65 all cells reach EDD=3 — the recursive signal is universally present, the question is how stringently we measure it

## 5. Feature Importance

### 5.1 Universal Feature Ranking (across 8 cells)

| Rank | Feature | Mean Importance | CV |
|------|---------|----------------|----|
| 1 | p90_ppl | 0.189 ± 0.039 | 0.21 |
| 2 | var_surprisal | 0.169 ± 0.022 | 0.13 |
| 3 | p75_ppl | 0.098 ± 0.029 | 0.29 |
| 4 | mean_surprisal | 0.095 ± 0.023 | 0.24 |
| 5 | mean_ppl | 0.057 ± 0.049 | 0.86 |

The core features **p90_ppl** and **var_surprisal** consistently rank in top-5 across all 8 cells, demonstrating stable feature importance across models and decoding strategies.

> **Note on per-cell deviations**:
> - *Pythia cells*: all three Pythia configurations place **mean_ppl** in top-3 instead of p75_ppl (universal rank 3). This shifts p75_ppl to rank 5 within Pythia.
> - *GPT-2 XL temp09*: **var_surprisal** ranks 4th (not top-3), displaced by mean_surprisal which rises to rank 2 in this cell. p50_ppl enters the top-5.

### 5.2 Per-Cell Top-5

| Cell | #1 | #2 | #3 | #4 | #5 |
|------|----|----|----|----|-----|
| pythia_nucleus | var_surprisal | p90_ppl | mean_ppl | mean_surprisal | p75_ppl |
| pythia_temp09 | var_surprisal | p90_ppl | mean_ppl | mean_surprisal | p75_ppl |
| pythia_topk50 | var_surprisal | p90_ppl | mean_ppl | mean_surprisal | p75_ppl |
| olmo_nucleus | p90_ppl | var_surprisal | p75_ppl | mean_surprisal | type_token_ratio |
| olmo_temp09 | p90_ppl | var_surprisal | p75_ppl | mean_surprisal | p50_ppl |
| olmo_topk50 | p90_ppl | var_surprisal | p75_ppl | mean_surprisal | p25_ppl |
| gpt2xl_nucleus | p90_ppl | var_surprisal | p75_ppl | mean_surprisal | mean_ppl |
| gpt2xl_temp09 | p90_ppl | mean_surprisal | p75_ppl | var_surprisal | p50_ppl |

### 5.3 Cross-Model Consistency

- Top-5 Jaccard similarity across all cells: 0.75 ± 0.14
- Nucleus strategy yields highest cross-model agreement (mean ρ=0.80)
- The feature set is stable despite per-cell rank permutations

## 6. Monotonicity

- 16/19 features show perfect monotonicity (|score|=1.0) across all 8 cells
- Perplexity/surprisal features: consistent downward monotonicity (values decrease with depth)
- Repetition features (rep_2gram, rep_3gram, rep_4gram): consistent upward monotonicity (more repetition at deeper depths)

## 7. Data Completeness

### 7.1 Cell Status

| Cell | Status | Experiment ID |
|------|--------|--------------|
| pythia_nucleus | ✓ Complete | mvp_pipeline_pythia_002 |
| pythia_temp09 | ✓ Complete | pythia_temp09_001 |
